# Introduction

Following @Bravec2023, we want to extract from ddRAD-seq FASTQ files all reads
that map to either the *cox1* gene or the lsrDNA, which are important markers
to discriminate flatworm species [@BlascoCosta2016].

First, I need the genomic sequences of the *cox1* gene and the lsrDNA, from our
*Crepidostomum* draft assembly. For that, I will turn the genome draft assembly
into a BLAST database, and I will use the closest *cox1* and lsrDNA available in
the databases as queries.

The *lsrDNA* is the long subunit ribosomal RNA gene, also known as LSU rRNA gene.
It is easier to find these sequences in the SILVA database than in the European
Nucleotide Archive.

The *cox1* gene is the cytochrome C oxidase subunit 1 gene, also known as COI.
Isabel made us note that ENA and GenBank have some more *Crepidostomum* *cox1*
sequences, including two from *C. farionis*, which could improve sensitivity.

# COX1

```{bash cox1Crepi}

if [ ! -e CrepiCoxENA.fa ]; then
   if [ ! -e accessions.txt ]; then
   ## COI
      PORTAL="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?"
      RESULT="result=sequence&"
      QUERY="query=tax_tree(334452)%20AND%20description%3D%22coi%22&"
      FIELDS="fields=accession%2Cscientific_name&"
      FORMAT="format=tsv"
      curl -s $PORTAL$RESULT$QUERY$FIELDS$FORMAT >> accessions.txt
   ## COX1
      PORTAL="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?"
      RESULT="result=sequence&"
      QUERY="query=tax_tree(334452)%20AND%20description%3D%22cox1%22&"
      FIELDS="fields=accession%2Cscientific_name&"
      FORMAT="format=tsv"
      curl -s $PORTAL$RESULT$QUERY$FIELDS$FORMAT | tail -n +2 >> accessions.txt
      # if I do Coi and Cox1 at the same time add this | tail -n +2 
   fi
   BROWSER="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/api/fasta/"
   cut -f 1 accessions.txt | tail -n +2 > accessions1.txt
   ACCESSIONS=$(gawk -v ORS="," '{print}' accessions1.txt |  sed 's/.$//' )
   curl -s $BROWSER$ACCESSIONS > CrepiCoxENA.fa
fi
```

```{r alignment1, message=FALSE}
library('DECIPHER')
library('htmltools')
cox1 <- c(readDNAStringSet('CrepiCoxENA.fa'))

# Flatworm mitochondrial code is table 9.
cox1.ali1 <- AlignTranslation(cox1, type = 'AAStringSet',
                              geneticCode = getGeneticCode('9'),
                              verbose = FALSE)
BrowseSeqs(cox1.ali1, htmlFile = 'cox1.ali1.html')
includeHTML('cox1.ali1.html')
z <- file.remove('cox1.ali1.html')
```

I realize most sequences are much shorter than a few longer ones. I keep 8 sequences, 
the largest ones. After checking that all translations would be the same frame, 
I use `AlignTranslation()` to make sure I am aligning codons.

```{r alignment2, warning=FALSE, eval = FALSE}
cox1 <- cox1[cox1@ranges@width > 600]
cox1.ali2 <- AlignTranslation(cox1, type = 'DNAStringSet',
                              geneticCode = getGeneticCode('9'),
                              verbose = FALSE)
# Shortening names
ena <- startsWith(names(cox1.ali2), 'ENA')
names(cox1.ali2)[! ena] <- sapply(strsplit(names(cox1.ali2)[! ena], "[\\|_]"),
                                  function(x) paste0('C.', x[[3]], '_', x[[1]]))
names(cox1.ali2)[  ena] <- sapply(strsplit(names(cox1.ali2)[  ena], "[\\| ]"),
                                  function(x) paste0('C.', x[[5]], '_', x[[2]]))
BrowseSeqs(cox1.ali2, htmlFile = 'cox1.ali2.html')
includeHTML('cox1.ali2.html')
z <- file.remove('cox1.ali2.html')

Queries <- DNAStringSet(gsub('-', '', cox1.ali2))
writeXStringSet(c(unique(Queries), readDNAStringSet("../../data/SeqCox1_Crepido_spp_Kristine.fas"), readDNAStringSet("../../data/SeqCox1_Crepido_spp_Isabel.fa")), filepath = 'cox1.queries.fasta')

library(ape)
cox1.ali3 <- as.DNAbin(unique(cox1.ali2))
cox1.dist <- dist.dna(cox1.ali3)
cox1.tree <- nj(cox1.dist)
plot(root(cox1.tree,
          outgroup = cox1.tree$tip.label[startsWith(cox1.tree$tip.label, 'C.illinoiense')]),
     font = 1)
```

## BLASTN
I created a consensus DNA sequence among all known *Crepidostomum* *cox1*
genes, to use it as a query in a BLASTN search againt the assembly. I also
extracted the *C. farionis* cox1 sequence to a FASTA file.

```{bash balstn}
ASSEMBLY="../2023-05-12/ABYSS_assembly/k90-kc2"
if [ ! -e Crepidostomum.ndb ]; then
   makeblastdb -in $ASSEMBLY/farionis-scaffolds.fa \
               -input_type 'fasta' \
               -title Crepidostomum \
               -out Crepidostomum \
               -dbtype 'nucl'
fi

if [ ! -e cox1_blastn.html ]; then
   blastn -db Crepidostomum \
          -query cox1.queries.fasta \
          -out cox1_blastn.html \
          -evalue 30 \
          -html
fi

if [ ! -e cox1_blastn.out ]; then
   blastn -db Crepidostomum \
          -query cox1.queries.fasta \
          -out cox1_blastn.out \
          -outfmt "7 qseqid sseqid slen qstart qend sstart send evalue" \
          -evalue 1
fi
```

```{r blastnout}
library(kableExtra)
#includeHTML('cox1_blastn.html')
blastn <- read.table('cox1_blastn.out',
                     col.names = c('qseqid', 'sseqid', 'slen', 'qstart', 'qend', 'sstart', 'send', 'evalue'))
blastn <- blastn[order(blastn$qstart),]
kable(blastn) %>% kable_styling()
```

Because BLASTN is not as sensitive as TBLASTN, the only query that reports
a hit along the whole sequence is that from *C. farionis*.

Curiously, we find 2 contigs that encode homologs of the COX1 protein, both
of approximately 14000 bases. This suggests we have two alternative mitochondrial
assemblies. Let's compare them.

## Extraction COI of the draft genome

```{bash}
## Clean the horrible names of the "contigs", and necessary to load it in R 
ASM=../2023-05-12/ABYSS_assembly/k90-kc2/farionis-scaffolds.fa
if [ ! -e farionis-scaffolds-clean.fa ]; then
  awk '/^>/{gsub(" .*", "", $0); print $0; next} {gsub(">", ""); print $0}' $ASM > farionis-scaffolds-clean.fa
fi
```


```{r cox1ref}
assembly <- readDNAStringSet("farionis-scaffolds-clean.fa")

Cox1Ref <- DNAStringSet(
  paste0(subseq(assembly['11399550'], 1, 179),
         subseq(assembly['6181713'], 13, 179), 
         subseq(assembly['15515475'], 66, 173),
         subseq(assembly['9054047'], 5, 179),
         subseq(assembly['15800549'], 18, 152),
         subseq(assembly['451844'], 1, 131),
         subseq(assembly['14625016'], 88, 126)
    )
)

names(Cox1Ref) <- 'Cox1'
writeXStringSet(Cox1Ref, 'Cox1Ref.fa', append = FALSE, format = 'fasta')
writeXStringSet(Cox1Ref, 'markersRef.fa', append = FALSE, format = 'fasta')
```

# LSU rRNA
I know, it didn't need to download the whole SILVA database to get only a few
sequences, but it's done.

```{bash silva}
#if [ ! -e lsrDNA.fasta ]; then
   if [ ! -e SILVA_138.1_LSURef_NR99_tax_silva_trunc.fasta.gz ]; then
      wget https://www.arb-silva.de/fileadmin/silva_databases/release_138.1/Exports/SILVA_138.1_LSURef_NR99_tax_silva_trunc.fasta.gz 2> /dev/null
   fi
#fi
```

The SILVA database produces a lsrDNA a bit different for those of
GenBank for the Crepidostomum species, so I'm going to use as 
query oonly the sequences of *C.farionis* and *C.pseudofarionis* from 
GenBank (ENA)
```{r lsrTrematoda, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
SILVA <- 'SILVA_138.1_LSURef_NR99_tax_silva_trunc.fasta.gz'
silva <- readRNAStringSet(SILVA)
# Plagiorchiida is the order to which Crepidistomum belongs.
Plagiorchiida <- silva[grep('Plagiorchiida', names(silva))]
# I build a consensus to simplify BLAST results
Plagiorchiida <- DNAStringSet(Plagiorchiida)
writeXStringSet(Plagiorchiida, 'lsrDNA.fasta')
z <- file.remove('SILVA_138.1_LSURef_NR99_tax_silva_trunc.fasta.gz')
```

```{bash}
## Sequences of farionis and pseudofarionis from GenBank
if [ ! -d Genbank ]; then mkdir Genbank; fi
if [ ! -e Genbank/INFO_28S_accessions.txt ]; then
   # farionis
   ## large subunit ribosomal
      PORTAL="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?"
      RESULT="result=sequence&"
      QUERY="query=tax_tree(984080)%20AND%20description%3D%22large%20subunit%20ribosomal%20%22&"
      FIELDS="fields=accession%2Cscientific_name%2Chost%2Ccountry%2Ctax_id&"
      FORMAT="format=tsv"
      curl -s $PORTAL$RESULT$QUERY$FIELDS$FORMAT >> Genbank/INFO_28S_accessions.txt
   ## 28S
      PORTAL="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?"
      RESULT="result=sequence&"
      QUERY="query=tax_tree(984080)%20AND%20description%3D%2228S%22&"
      FIELDS="fields=accession%2Cscientific_name%2Chost%2Ccountry%2Ctax_id&"
      FORMAT="format=tsv"
      curl -s $PORTAL$RESULT$QUERY$FIELDS$FORMAT | tail -n +2 >> Genbank/INFO_28S_accessions.txt
   # pseudofarionis
   ## large subunit ribosomal
      PORTAL="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?"
      RESULT="result=sequence&"
      QUERY="query=tax_tree(2710753)%20AND%20description%3D%22large%20subunit%20ribosomal%20%22&"
      FIELDS="fields=accession%2Cscientific_name%2Chost%2Ccountry%2Ctax_id&"
      FORMAT="format=tsv"
      curl -s $PORTAL$RESULT$QUERY$FIELDS$FORMAT | tail -n +2 >> Genbank/INFO_28S_accessions.txt
   ## 28S
      PORTAL="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?"
      RESULT="result=sequence&"
      QUERY="query=tax_tree(2710753)%20AND%20description%3D%2228S%22&"
      FIELDS="fields=accession%2Cscientific_name%2Chost%2Ccountry%2Ctax_id&"
      FORMAT="format=tsv"
      curl -s $PORTAL$RESULT$QUERY$FIELDS$FORMAT | tail -n +2 >> Genbank/INFO_28S_accessions.txt
      # if I do Coi and Cox1 at the same time add this | tail -n +2 
   fi
   BROWSER="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/api/fasta/"
   cut -f 1 Genbank/INFO_28S_accessions.txt | tail -n +2 > Genbank/accessions_28S.txt
   ACCESSIONS=$(gawk -v ORS="," '{print}' Genbank/accessions_28S.txt |  sed 's/.$//' )
   curl -s $BROWSER$ACCESSIONS > Genbank/Crepi28S_REFS.fa


```

## BLASTN

```{bash blastn2}
if [ ! -e lsrDNA_blastn.html ]; then
   blastn -db Crepidostomum \
          -query Genbank/Crepi28S_REFS.fa \
          -out lsrDNA_blastn.html \
          -evalue 10 \
          -num_alignments 15 \
          -html
fi

if [ ! -e lsrDNA_blastn.out ]; then
   blastn -db Crepidostomum \
          -query Genbank/Crepi28S_REFS.fa \
          -out lsrDNA_blastn.out \
          -outfmt "7 qseqid sseqid slen qstart qend sstart send evalue" \
          -evalue 1
fi
```

```{r blastn2out}
library(kableExtra)
includeHTML('lsrDNA_blastn.html')
blastn <- read.table('lsrDNA_blastn.out',
                     col.names = c('qseqid', 'sseqid', 'slen', 'qstart', 'qend', 'sstart', 'send', 'evalue'))
blastn <- blastn[order(blastn$qstart),]
kable(blastn) %>% kable_styling()
```

Homology to lsrDNA is distributed among several contigs. It is not surprising that
ribosomal DNA didn't get assembled correctly, because it is highly repetitive. I
assume different copies undergo concerted evolution [@DeLuca2021] and are similar
enough to put the pieces together.

```{bash}
## Clean the horrible names of the "contigs", and necessary to load it in R 
ASM=../2023-05-12/ABYSS_assembly/k90-kc2/farionis-scaffolds.fa
if [ ! -e farionis-scaffolds-clean.fa ]; then
  awk '/^>/{gsub(" .*", "", $0); print $0; next} {gsub(">", ""); print $0}' $ASM > farionis-scaffolds-clean.fa
fi
```


```{r pasteSyn, eval=FALSE}
assembly <- readDNAStringSet("farionis-scaffolds-clean.fa")

BrowseSeqs(subseq(assembly["18044708"]))
BrowseSeqs(subseq(assembly["18195207"]))

lsrDNARef <- DNAStringSet(
  paste0(subseq(assembly['18044708'], 1827, 4681),
     reverseComplement(subseq(assembly['18195207'], 2954, 3954))
    )
)

names(lsrDNARef) <- 'Synthetic_lsrDNA_ref'
BrowseSeqs(AlignSeqs(c(lsrDNARef, readDNAStringSet("Genbank/Crepi28S_REFS.fa"))))

writeXStringSet(lsrDNARef, 'Syn_lsrDNARef.fa', append = TRUE)
#writeXStringSet(lsrDNARef, 'markers.fa', append = TRUE)
```

assembly <- readDNAStringSet("farionis-scaffolds-clean.fa")

lsrDNARef1 <- DNAStringSet(paste0(subseq(assembly['18044708'], 1830, 3205))) ## far
lsrDNARef2 <- DNAStringSet(paste0(subseq(assembly['18192530'], 4068, 5428))) ## far
lsrDNARef3 <- DNAStringSet(paste0(subseq(assembly['18096606'], 7047, 8405))) ## far
lsrDNARef4 <- DNAStringSet(paste0(reverseComplement(subseq(assembly['17772478'], 3147, 4409)))) ## far
lsrDNARef5 <- DNAStringSet(paste0(reverseComplement(subseq(assembly['18016522'], 710, 2082)))) ## far
lsrDNARef6 <- DNAStringSet(paste0(reverseComplement(subseq(assembly['4240400'], 1, 894)))) ## far

#lsrDNARef6 <- DNAStringSet(paste0(subseq(assembly['16124017'], 137, 691))) ## far
#lsrDNARef7 <- DNAStringSet(paste0(subseq(assembly['18096606'], 7047, 8405))) ## far

# Conclusions
Keep in mind the COI is the result of my own manually pasting together 
the pieces from diffrent contigs. Again, reads mapping to the joints 
would confirm the reconstruction is correct. Good luck.

At the end, we have two sequences for lsrDNA. One make by all the SILVA
database, Syn_lsrDNARef.fa, and the other only with the lsrDNA from 
Crepidostomum farionis and pseudofarionis specimens. 
The Syn_lsrDNARef.fa will be used for the mapping of our all samples, 
while the lsrDNARef.fa will be used for the phylogenetic reconstruction. 
This is an approach to obtain all the bases we can in the alignment and 
consensus steps for the samples.
